19886.description: An 8 ns simulation of the 6kqi PDB entries which includes Uniprot entry: P21554. The simulation was produced using the MISATO automated pipeline. The MISATO dataset provides a large-scale, high-quality resource of ~19,400 experimentally determined protein–ligand complexes curated from PDBbind, each corrected for structural errors with semi-empirical quantum mechanical refinements and enriched with computed quantum chemical properties. To capture conformational flexibility, the authors generated explicit all-atom molecular dynamics simulations in water; each run was 10 ns but only the final 8 ns were saved as trajectories. For every system, Amber restart and topology files are available, along with Gromacs-formatted topology, structure, and PDB files for the full solvated system. The saved trajectories include only protein and ligand atoms, and are accompanied by corresponding `cleaned' Gromacs topology, structure, and PDB files with water and ions removed. Each trajectory contains 100 frames at 800 ps intervals, and per-frame analyses such as buried solvent-accessible surface area (bSASA), protein–ligand center-of-mass distance, interaction energy, and ligand RMSD are available in CSV format. The external link (https://zenodo.org/records/7711953) refers to the location of the full set of MISATO simulations; retrieval of this single simulation from that zenodo record requires download of the entire payload, followed by extract using a script such as those provided at https://github.com/t7morgen/misato-dataset/tree/master/src/data/processing (though MDRepo provides direct access the full contents of all records).

90076.description: All-atom molecular dynamics of the protein-ligand complex 6n4b bound to CCD component KCA, drawn from the PLAS-20K dataset. This submission bundles 5 independent replica trajectories that share one topology. Each replica covers 0-3900 ps of production sampling at 100 ps between frames (40 frames). System: 5020 atoms across 304 residues, of which 53 belong to the ligand. The ligand net charge is +0, summed from the partial charges in the authors' own topology -- i.e. the charge the trajectory was generated with, not one inferred from a reference entry. Solvent has been stripped: the deposited trajectories contain protein, ligand and any cofactors only. The underlying simulation was run fully solvated in TIP3P. The source replica files carry the solute plus the two crystal waters the authors selected as the closest to both protein and ligand; those two waters are stripped here, and the source files contain no counter-ions to strip. Trajectories are deposited in mdcompress (.mdc) format at a coordinate resolution of 1000 fm (0.01 Angstrom). This compression is lossy in the same sense that the .xtc format is: positions are quantised, and the quantum is far below both the thermal fluctuation of the underlying sampling and the precision of the source coordinates. Every replica was decompressed and compared frame by frame against the uncompressed original before submission; the deviation is reported per complex in the QC record. The AMBER topology accompanying this submission is the ORIGINAL INVESTIGATORS' OWN BUILD, not a reconstruction. The published dataset ships coordinates only, but the authors separately released their topologies, and this is theirs: the protein+ligand system of their own tleap build (leaprc.protein.ff14SB + leaprc.gaff2, ligand and cofactor parameters from antechamber GAFF2/AM1-BCC), with the two crystal waters they carried in their solute unit removed to match the deposited trajectories. Nothing in it was recomputed here. Consequently the parameters are the ones the trajectory was actually generated with, rather than an equivalent rebuilt under a later AmberTools whose GAFF2 differs by up to 0.55 e on ligand charges. The correspondence was not assumed: every complex passed an automated QC gate (atom/residue/element sequence identity against the trajectory, bond-length sanity on each replica, and coordinate round-trip fidelity through both the NetCDF conversion and the mdc compression), and complexes whose released topology disagreed with their own trajectory were rejected rather than repaired. Source data: PLAS-20K (Korlepara et al., Scientific Data 11, 180 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02872-y), produced by IIIT Hyderabad (devalab) and distributed by IIIT-H / iHub-Data. Upstream copy used: version2 (india-data.org PLAS-20K-Variation2 mirror).
90076.short_description: PLAS-20K protein-ligand MD ensemble for PDB 6n4b bound to KCA: 5 replica trajectories of 40 frames, protein and ligand only, with the original investigators' AMBER topology.
90076.run_commands: Production dynamics were run by the original investigators, not by this pipeline: OpenMM 7.2.0 (doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02872-y). OpenMM is absent from MDRepo's software vocabulary, so software_name records the AMBER convention the deposited topology follows. The topology is the authors' own tleap build, republished here rather than reconstructed; the authors published no AmberTools version, and their topology files were written between 2021 and 2023.

104079.description: Enhanced-sampling all-atom molecular dynamics dissociation trajectory for the 6kqi protein-ligand complex, which includes Uniprot entry P21554 bound to ligand 2-[(1R,2R,5R)-5-hydroxy-2-(3-hydroxypropyl)cyclohexyl]-5-(2-methyloctan-2-yl)phenol. The simulation is one of 50 replicates for this complex, produced using the DD-03B pipeline of the Dissociation Dynamic Database (DDD) project. DD-03B is a large-scale dynamic resource that provides all-atom dissociation trajectories for 15440 ligand-protein complexes sourced from PDBbind+v2020.R1 free, totaling approximately 0.3 billion simulation frames and ~39.9 TB of data.  To induce ligand egress without requiring a predefined reaction coordinate, we applied metadynamics (MetaD) with a three-dimensional collective variable defined by the Cartesian coordinates of the ligand center-of-mass; each run terminates as soon as the ligand COM crosses the protein surface, which serves as the committor boundary. For each complex, multiple parallel MetaD runs with different random seeds were performed, yielding an ensemble of independent dissociation pathways. Simulations were carried out in explicit solvent using the same computational pipeline using the SPONGE MD engine.
